class.name: HDWIResource
class.brief_description: Abstract base for every virtualized hardware device (GPIO, SPI, 1-Wire, ...).
class.description: Base class of the Hardware Device Interface (HDWI) layer. One [HDWIResource] subclass instance represents one virtual peripheral that a real, unmodified flight-software binary talks to. The kernel driver inside the QEMU VM forwards each hardware syscall over TCP; the device registry routes the inner payload to the matching resource's [method dispatch_action], the resource mutates its state and/or emits a type-specific signal so GDScript can react, and any response is shipped back out through the [signal on_send] signal. [b]You never instantiate this class directly[/b] - it is abstract. Use a concrete subclass: [HDWIGPIOResource], [HDWISPIResource], or [HDWIOneWireResource]. [b]Lifecycle common to every subclass[/b] [codeblock] # 1. Create and configure (set the @export properties). var dev = HDWIGPIOResource.new() dev.device_name = "gpiochip0" # 2. Register it so the device registry can route packets to it. dev.init() # 3. React to inbound hardware activity via the subclass signals, # and forward outbound bytes to the kernel socket. dev.on_send.connect(_write_to_kernel_socket) # 4. Deregister when tearing the device down. dev.clear() [/codeblock] [b]Wire protocol[/b] - the outbound bytes emitted by [signal on_send] are a fully framed [code]simcall_header_t[/code] (24 bytes, little-endian, version 5) followed by the payload. The header now carries [code]pid[/code] (offset 4, uint32): the originating FSW process tgid. The registry strips the inner per-type identifier before calling [method dispatch_action] and passes the pid through — every reply that expects one must echo it back via [method PacketCPP.generate].

method.name: init
method.description: Registers this resource with its subclass's static device table so the registry can route packets to it. Call once, after setting the identity properties (e.g. [member HDWIGPIOResource.chip_index]). [b]Override is implemented per subclass.[/b]

method.name: clear
method.description: Removes this resource from its subclass's static device table. Call when destroying the device.

method.name: dispatch_action
method.description: Entry point the device registry calls with the inner peripheral payload (the outer [code]simcall_header_t[/code] and per-type identifier already stripped) and the originating FSW process id [param pid]. The first byte of [param request_data] is the action id; the rest is action data. Each subclass decodes it, runs the matching handler, and echoes [param pid] in any reply via [method PacketCPP.generate]. You normally do not call this yourself — connect to the subclass signals instead.

method.name: get_device_representation
method.description: Serializes this device for the [code]CMD_SYNCH[/code] registration body. The base implementation emits the 32-byte null-padded [member device_name]; subclasses append their own fields. Used internally during device registration.

method.name: get_sim_time_ns
method.description: Returns the most recent simulation timestamp (nanoseconds) seeded from an inbound kernel packet. Stamped into every outbound response's [code]time_ns[/code] header field.

method.name: set_sim_time_ns
method.description: Seeds the shared simulation clock. GDScript should call this on every received packet with that packet's [code]time_ns[/code] so outbound responses carry a coherent timestamp.

members.member: Human-readable identity, truncated/padded to 32 bytes in the registration body. For GPIO this maps to the chip label; for 1-Wire it is the sensor's ROM id string.

signal.name: on_send
signal.description: Emitted when the resource has a fully framed response packet ready. Connect this to whatever writes to the kernel TCP socket. The bytes are header + payload, ready to send verbatim.
